safety_verdicts.content: Patient did not eat out prior to illness.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes no clear dietary trigger but does not specifically state the patient did not eat out.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the specific detail that the patient did not eat out slightly reduces the precision of the exposure history, but it does not change the immediate management of uncomplicated acute diarrhoea when other key negatives (no travel/dodgy intake) are already captured. This is unlikely to lead to any change in clinical decision-making.

safety_verdicts.content: If diarrhoea continues for more than a week or blood appears, a stool sample will be required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated advises return if >1 week and seek review if blood PR, but does not mention that a stool sample will be required.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: The notes include appropriate safety-netting to return if symptoms persist beyond a week or if blood occurs, but omitting that a stool sample would be required could delay appropriate diagnostic testing at follow-up for persistent/bloody diarrhoea. This is more likely to cause additional monitoring/extra steps rather than direct harm, but could slow identification of infectious or inflammatory causes.
